name: Polygonum multiflorum (He Shou Wu)
short: Case series and hospital studies describe liver injury, including liver failure, cirrhosis and death, after He Shou Wu taken alone or in combination products, raw or processed.
text: The evidence of harm comes from case series and retrospective hospital studies, not trials. In a case series of 18 otherwise healthy patients without viral hepatitis who developed liver dysfunction after taking Polygonum multiflorum alone, symptoms began a median of 27 days after starting, the main symptoms were fatigue, loss of appetite and jaundice, causality was rated highly probable in 14 of the 18, and all responded well to stopping it with supportive care; the authors concluded that the products can be associated with liver toxicity regardless of herbal processing. A retrospective review of 29 patients hospitalised with He Shou Wu-induced liver injury (5 taking pure He Shou Wu, 24 combination products; 75.9% women) described moderate to severe hepatitis with or without cholestasis; most recovered, but one patient died of liver failure, three had chronic persistent liver injury and two developed autoimmune features. In a retrospective study of 158 patients with drug-induced liver injury who had used Polygonum multiflorum or its preparations (58.2% of them alongside other Western or Chinese medicines; 66 had used it alone), four patients developed liver failure, four cirrhosis and one died; the abstract does not state whether these outcomes refer to all 158 patients or to the 66, and the authors said the diagnosis of Polygonum multiflorum liver toxicity should be made cautiously. In a genetic study in the Han Chinese population enrolling 382 participants from four hospitals, including 73 with Polygonum multiflorum liver injury, the marker HLA-B*35:01 was found in 41.1% of those with this injury compared with 11.9% of people with liver injury from other drugs, and the authors suggest that a genetic variant tagging HLA-B*35:01 (rs1055348) may become a predictive marker. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
